title: Approximate majorization and high-order capacity of quantum depolarizing channels
authors: Zhiwei Song, Xin Wang, Marco Tomamichel, Kun Fang
abstract: A central challenge in quantum information theory is to determine whether entanglement provides an advantage for information processing when coherent operations across multiple channel uses are allowed. For depolarizing channels, King's proof of the additivity of the minimum output entropy rules out such an advantage for classical communication at leading asymptotic order, while leaving open the possibility of an advantage for higher orders. In this work, we conjecture a majorization relation for the outputs of depolarizing channels and prove an approximate version of this conjecture. Our proof combines an exact ordering of shifted log-determinants with an anti-concentration bound for the spectrum of the product-state output, refining King's analysis based on Schatten norms. As a direct application, we obtain a tight third-order expansion for the classical capacity of quantum depolarizing channels. Consequently, entangled codewords and collective decoding can improve the message size over the product-coding strategy by at most $O(\log \log n)$ bits, sharpening our understanding of the role of entanglement in the finite-blocklength regime.
summary: This work tackles the question of entanglement advantage in quantum communication using depolarizing channels. By proving an approximate majorization relation for the channel outputs, the authors derive a precise third-order expansion for the classical capacity. This shows that while entanglement offers some improvement over product coding, this advantage is sub-logarithmic in the blocklength $n$.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether entanglement provides an advantage for classical communication capacity when using multiple uses of quantum depolarizing channels in the finite-blocklength regime.
main_result: They prove an approximate majorization relation for the channel outputs, leading to a tight third-order expansion showing that entanglement improves the message size by at most $O(\log \log n)$ bits over product coding.
method: The analysis combines proving an approximate majorization relation using log-determinant orderings with established quantum information theory bounds (like the hypothesis-testing meta-converse).
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the quantum depolarizing channel, $D_{p,d}$, applied over $n$ uses. The core mathematical tools involve majorization ($\prec$), spectral defects ($\delta_{	ext{maj}}$), and log-determinant functionals.
key_observables: Classical capacity ($c_{d,p}$), spectral defect ($\delta_{	ext{maj}}$), and the message size $\log M^*(n, \varepsilon)$.
important_parameters: Depolarizing parameter ($p$), blocklength ($n$), and error tolerance ($\varepsilon$).
main_assumptions: The authors conjecture a full majorization relation but only prove an approximate version, which is sufficient for the third-order capacity expansion.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing necessary spectral orderings (log-determinant) to proving an approximate majorization bound, which is then directly applied in the context of quantum channel capacity to derive the finite-blocklength expansion.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical tools developed (majorization, log-determinant ordering) provide powerful, non-standard ways to quantify resource advantages (like entanglement) in quantum communication protocols, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems theory.
